newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia gains further on Lehman report.
newsitem.headline: Nokia gains further on Lehman report.

text.p: Shares in Finnish telecoms group Nokia Oy powered ahead in active trade on Wednesday following news Lehman Brothers had named Nokia as one of eight continental European stocks expected to outperform in 1997, brokers said.
At 1525/1325 GMT Nokia was up 18.00 markka or over 6.6 percent at 290.00 markka, clearly surpassing its 279.00 markka close in New York on Tuesday.
Turnover in Nokia shares was heavy at over 270 million markka accounting for 52 percent of total bourse volume and brokers said demand was mainly generated from overseas.
Firm resistance for Nokia was seen at 300.00 markka, brokers said.
"The psychological resistance level for Nokia is 300.00 markka -- that it is a level were we could see profit-taking by domestic investors," said Panu Saukkonen, options broker at Arctos Securities.
Saukkonen said the following resistance level would be Nokia's 340.00 markka life-high, recorded in September 1995.
He expected Nokia to peak once more on Wednesday, but said it was unlikely to test 300.00 markka yet.
Postipankki analyst Ilkka Salonen said Nokia was "still very cheap" compared to its rivals U.S. Motorola and Swedish Ericsson.
